author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to footage of a British teenager having his flag physically taken from him, calling it British kids having their national identity ripped from their hands in a visceral and visible way. He reflects on how flags have carried different meanings throughout his own life, from skepticism about their inclusivity to seeing them worn and waved by figures like Morrissey and Oasis, before landing on the real question, what does it actually mean when a flag gets snatched out of a 16 year old's hand.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell responds to backlash over Billie Eilish's mansion reportedly sitting on land once occupied by the Tongva tribe, who say she never reached out to them directly, all while she's publicly said things like "no one is illegal on stolen land." Russell argues this exposes a deeper problem with performative wokeness itself, warning that fame turns on people fast the moment they slip up or stop being useful. He gets candid about his own time at events like the Grammys and MTV Awards, admitting something always felt off about the whole spectacle.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to a man being questioned by British police over comments he allegedly made, telling someone to speak clearly, only for it to come out he's partially deaf and couldn't actually hear the other person. Officers still tell him it could potentially be perceived as a hate crime. Russell's blunt takeaway, this doesn't look like a police force acting with integrity on behalf of the British people.
